title: Porosity Induction in a Mn3O4 Nanoparticle Assisted by the Time Exposition to Energy of Electron Beam in TEM
content: The exploration of atomic manipulation at the nanoscale has garnered significant attention from the scientific community in recent years [1]. This growing interest stems from the transformative potential of such strategies to enable the miniaturization of devices, particularly in the field of electronics. By achieving precise control over atomic and molecular structures, researchers can unlock new opportunities to design and fabricate electronic devices with unprecedented performance and functionality. These advances are critical for meeting the ever-increasing demand for smaller, faster, and more efficient technologies in a wide range of industries [2]. Among the various materials studied for nanoscale manipulation, metal oxide compounds present unique challenges and opportunities. These materials often exhibit strong chemical bonds, which makes their precise modification at the atomic level particularly difficult. The processes required to disrupt these bonds typically involve specialized chemical reagents or advanced physical techniques. Despite these challenges, the ability to manipulate metal oxides at such small scales is of great interest due to their versatile properties, including thermal stability, catalytic activity, and electronic characteristics. These properties make them promising candidates for a wide range of applications, from catalysis to energy storage and beyond. In this context, the Mn3O4 phase stands out as a material of particular interest. Recent studies have identified Mn3O4 as a highly functional compound with unique properties that extend its applications beyond traditional catalysis. For instance, it has been reported to act as a non-catalytic reactor, a feature that facilitates its integration into advanced nanodevices. Such devices have demonstrated potential for applications in critical areas, including environmental remediation through pollutant degradation, CO2 reduction to mitigate climate change effects, and localized hyperthermia therapy for cancer treatment [3, 4]. This study focuses on exploring atomic migration within Mn3O4 nanoparticles, a phenomenon that occurs when these particles are exposed to the electron beam of a transmission electron microscope (TEM). The investigation specifically examined the influence of exposure time to the electron beam and its resulting effects on the structural integrity and chemical composition of the Mn3O4 nanoparticles. By systematically varying the exposure duration, the study sought to elucidate the relationship between electron beam interaction and atomic behavior. These findings are expected to contribute to the broader understanding of atomic manipulation in metal oxides, paving the way for improved design and application of nanoscale devices in various scientific and technological fields.
